name: Span and Spirit
_what: Info film for the Span and Spirit domain: the Horizon-Walkers, the Hourkeepers and the Numinous, their homes, schools, cults, costs, a hero each where canon has one, and the arguments across their axes. Written to films/BRIEF.md.

lines: Span and Spirit.
Three peoples who will not take distance, duration or matter as given.
The waygates and the archives that run forward are Precursor works.
Span walks on someone else's road.
Spirit needs meaning to work on, and the places thick with meaning are usually thick with lattice too.
The Long Span moves: tents, roads and carts, open country ahead.
The Horizon-Walkers have no fixed anything, and think that a completed thought.
Distance is a claim. Argue with it long enough and it gives.
Their one fixed house is the Wayhouse, and they are embarrassed by it.
Its gate stands in the yard, unfenced and unwatched.
Walkers know the road. Spanners fold it.
after: The Leavers take a party into the far country, and fold out without them.

lines: The Unlanded have walked so long they cannot stop.
Meeting them on a road is one of the loneliest things there is.
Past the edge of the map there is no quick way back.
Horizon-Walkers are famously bad at staying.
Aro of the Horizon Reach has never been hit on the Coliseum's sand.
He wants someone fast enough to make it a bout.
Lately the roads are longer. People who part are not meeting again.
The Horizon-Walker refuses distance. The Hourkeeper refuses duration.
Both are arguments with a limit, and both eventually win.
The Slow Hour: clock-towers, all slightly out of step.
The Hourkeepers remember, and remember forward, and pay for both.
They are the saddest people in the world and among the kindest, because they know how much time everything has.
The Forward Archive files what has not happened yet.
The wrong entries are kept too. They are the most-read shelves.
Keepers give time. Watchers keep the long vigil.
after: The Hour-Thieves stretch a person's worst moment until it breaks them.

lines: The Stopped have held one hour so hard they are still inside it.
They have been in it for two hundred years.
Foreseeing binds: what you have seen changes what you do, and so changes what you saw.
The Numinous live at the Thinning, where the Veil is thin enough to feel.
Nothing there is set in foundations.
Attend to something completely enough, and the material softens around what it means.
At the Lampless Hermitage they sit for years doing what looks like nothing.
It is the hardest thing anyone in this world attempts.
Attenders hold meaning open. It must be there already: they gather it, and rarely make it.
after: The Dimmers take it out of a life, and leave the life working and empty.

lines: At the far end, the Numen: empty halls, and people gone too far into the practice to come back.
They are the most peaceful thing in the world. That is the problem.
Warden Isolde keeps the Green Accord at Thornwake Glade.
She tests intent before skill, and welcome before trust.
The Enginewright repairs what is broken. The Numinous hold open what is closing.
after: Now the Great Engine is waking old works the Numinous say must stay asleep.

lines: In the Slow Hour's council, one chair is always kept empty,
for someone who has not arrived yet.

title.line2: The far road, the long hour, the thin place
